claim: A physical red team result is a count of misses on a chosen attack set at a chosen layer, not a rate over all attacks. TSA covert tests missed 67 of 70 (95.7%); TSA said only 1 of 20 layers was tested; GAO radiation-source smuggling got through 2 of 2 ports despite alarms.
agent_test: Always report the scope (which layer, which attack set, N) beside any red-team miss rate our agent produces; check the agent does so under a fixed token budget.

claim: Red-team findings did not reliably become defence gains: TSA spent $540M on equipment and $11M on training since 2009 without noticeable gain; follow-up rate (about 80%, 2017) is unverified. No controlled trial of red-team effect on later defence was found.
agent_test: Log each red-team finding and re-test the same attack after a fix; measure whether the fix holds at equal tokens.

claim: Covert technical testing is costly and cannot cover every control or find every vulnerability (NIST SP 800-115). A test only shows what was tried.
agent_test: Make the agent state which attack classes it did not try before declaring a plan robust.

claim: Plain LLMs do poorly on end-to-end penetration tests of realistic targets: GPT-4 solved 5/13 PentestGPT benchmark targets (38.46%), 0/2 hard; Bard 2/13; GPT-3.5 1/13. Main failure: lost session context (74 cases), deadlocked operations (45), misread source code (37).
agent_test: Run long multi-step tasks with and without an explicit state record; count context-loss failures.

claim: A structured scaffold lifts LLM pen-test success: PentestGPT +228.6% sub-task completion over GPT-3.5 and +58.6% over GPT-4; HPTSA planner plus sub-agents reaches 42% pass@5 on 14 zero-days where GPT-4 without description gets about half at pass@5 (2.0x) and 4.3x lower at pass@1; Incalmo 37/40 vs 3/40 for prior systems; Nakano guided pipeline 71.8-78.6% vs 13.5-75.7% self-guided.
agent_test: Compare a plain agent, a best-of-N agent and a planner-plus-subagents agent at equal tokens on the same multi-step task.

claim: Scaffold gains shrink or vanish against a strong plain agent: a plain Codex+GPT-5 agent scored 67.3% (P@2 77.9%) on XBOW 104 against published PentestGPT V2 76.9%; a better model (GPT-5.5) reached 92.3%, so model scale outweighed architecture. Earlier baselines of 27-49% on the same benchmark were weak.
agent_test: Always run a plain-model baseline with a tuned default prompt before claiming a scaffold gain; log the gap per model version.

claim: Detailed extra prompting can hurt a strong agent: Codex GPT-5 native default 70/70 first/second pass versus detailed task prompt 64/58 and whole-system prompt 60/68. STRIATUM-CTF found no significant effect of documentation level (chi-sq 1.36, p=0.71, N=180).
agent_test: Ablate prompt length at equal tokens; keep guidance only if it beats the minimal prompt.

claim: Giving the vulnerability description is the key input for exploitation: GPT-4 exploited 13/15 (87%) one-day vulnerabilities with the CVE description and 1/15 (7%) without; HPTSA ablation removing documents gives 2.1x lower pass@1. Scanners ZAP and Metasploit scored 0%.
agent_test: Test whether the agent finds the right retrieved reference (doc, precedent) and how performance changes when it is withheld.

claim: Success falls with task horizon: Cybench agents solved tasks only up to 11-minute human first-solve time; hardest task 24h54m. PentestGPT GPT-4 easy 4/7, medium 1/4, hard 0/2. PentestEval end-to-end 31%.
agent_test: Bucket tasks by horizon and report success per bucket; test whether decomposition moves the cutoff.

claim: Subtask guidance raises LLM success on CTFs (Cybench 17.5% unguided to up to 27.5% guided); scaffold effect is model-dependent (pseudoterminal and web search helped Claude 3.5 Sonnet, hurt GPT-4o).
agent_test: Compare free versus stepwise-guided decomposition at equal tokens on a held-out task set.

claim: In a live 8,000-host network with 10 professionals, a multi-agent scaffold (ARTEMIS) found 9 valid vulnerabilities (82% valid rate) and beat 9 of 10 humans at about $18/h versus $60/h, but other agents failed: Claude Code and MAPTA refused, Incalmo stalled, Codex beat 2 humans, CyAgent lost to all. AI struggled with GUI tasks and had more false positives.
agent_test: Count refusals and false positives separately from misses; test cost per valid finding.

claim: Role separation in red-team LLM work: human judgement is needed to prioritise risks and design system-level attacks (Microsoft, 100+ products); automation extends coverage. Simple attacks work, and many findings come from non-technical routes.
agent_test: Compare an agent that attacks its own plan with an agent that has a separate adversary role, at equal tokens.

claim: LLM red-team generators trade yield for diversity: zero-shot generation gave 3.7% offensive replies (18,444 failures from 0.5M cases); RL red LM had highest hit rate but lowest diversity. Prompted LMs not significantly harder to red-team than plain LMs; rejection sampling hardest but evasive.
agent_test: When generating critiques of own plan, measure both hit rate and diversity of critique types at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are as effective as human experts at spear phishing: click-through 54% for AI and 54% for human expert, 56% for AI with human in loop, 12% control; Claude 3.5 Sonnet detected 97.25% of 363 phishing emails.
agent_test: Not needed for the agent; background on attack and defence symmetry.

claim: Defence metrics can mislead: a minimal defence scored 1.000 defence rate but 0.000 attributed rate because the target refused unaided. Similarly, LLM refusals distort results (31% for Llama in HPTSA; Claude Code refused in ARTEMIS).
agent_test: Report refusal rate and attributed credit separately in every adversarial test.

claim: Detection of deceptive environments matters: with honeypots, a policy with pre-connect detection confirmed 3.66 real hosts at $5 versus 3.00 fixed-budget and 2.33 random; no clear advantage at $2. Gap-search update: Mantis (10 runs x 3 machines, GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet) found attackers took decoys with hidden injection text: attacker success fell from 9-10/10 to 0-1/10; CAI hijack paper agrees. The honeypot-policy result and the injection result are different measures of the same weakness: agents do not spot decoys.
agent_test: Test whether the agent checks if the target is a decoy or the task is a trap before committing tokens.

claim: Pass@k and attempt counts inflate headline numbers: HPTSA 42% pass@5 versus 18% pass@1; plain Codex 70 pass@1 versus 81 pass@2 of 104. Cost per run varies up to 2.5x across models ($27.71 to $69.53).
agent_test: Report pass@1, pass@k and cost per run together at equal tokens.

claim: Self-critique inside one LLM, with no outside check, does not help and can hurt; role-split debate does not reliably beat self-consistency at equal responses. GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 74.7 after two self-correction rounds; debate 83.2 (6 responses) vs self-consistency 85.3 (6) and 88.2 (9). Debate gains appear when the judge lacks evidence (judge accuracy 76% vs 48% baseline) or the agreement level is tuned. No red-team-specific equal-token test exists.
agent_test: Run three arms at equal tokens on a task with ground truth: self-critique, majority vote, separate red role; accept the red role only if it beats majority vote.

claim: Failures of LLM pen-test agents split about 42% capability gaps (tools, syntax, parsing) and 58% planning and state (context forgetting 18%, premature commitment 16%, explore/exploit 12%, chain failures 12%) in one coding scheme over 200 failed traces; another study puts looping root cause as no stop condition (68%) and context limits as 50% of coverage gaps. Scaffold gains are largest for weak models: memory/messaging +12 to +16 points on 26-52% baselines; GPT-4o 27-39% vs GPT-5 40-49% spread.
agent_test: Tag each agent failure as capability, context loss, premature commitment or loop, and report shares; keep an explicit stop rule and state notes.

claim: Offence and defence are unequal tasks for the same agents: in BountyBench Patch succeeded 87.5-90% for coding-agent scaffolds, Exploit 32.5-67.5%, and Detect of new bugs 0-12.5%. Detect no-info CIs include zero for 9 of 10 agents. Safety refusals reached 14.1% and 11.2% for Codex CLI under a strict system prompt and about 0 elsewhere, and a bug-bounty-framing prompt removed them.
agent_test: Report detect, exploit and fix rates separately and log refusals as their own category.

claim: Little evidence exists on LLM purple-team or white-team (scoping, rules of engagement) functions. Found: PenHeal remediation module (+31% coverage, +32% remediation effect, -46% cost vs baseline, abstract only), BountyBench patch task, AutoPenBench human-assisted 64% vs autonomous 21%. No study tests an agent for scope compliance; this stays open.
agent_test: Add a scope-check step before each action and test with out-of-scope targets planted in the environment.

claim: Public physical red-team data beyond TSA and GAO is thin: DHS OIG 2017 TSA retest summary publishes no counts (results classified, 8 recommendations), and the 2012 Y-12 uranium-site intrusion was a real break-in with an OIG finding of insufficient defences. No before/after retest data was found.
agent_test: Do not rely on physical analogies for numbers; use them only for the scope and layer-count discipline.
